name: Spinach and pinto bean quesadillas
side: Salsa, sour cream and shredded lettuce.
mildNote: Leave out the chili powder and use mild salsa; the beans and cheese are kid-friendly on their own.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, chili powder and salt and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the pinto beans and 2 tbsp water, mash them roughly with a fork or potato masher and cook for 2 minutes, until thick.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until it wilts, about 2 minutes, then scrape the filling into a bowl and wipe out the skillet.
Spread the filling over half of each tortilla, top with the Monterey Jack and fold the tortillas in half.
Brush the skillet with a little of the remaining oil and cook the quesadillas two at a time over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with the salsa and sour cream.

name: Crispy skillet gnocchi with peas and parmesan
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and add half the gnocchi straight from the package in a single layer.
Cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, until golden underneath, then toss and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until crisp and puffed; tip into a bowl and repeat with the remaining oil and gnocchi.
Lower the heat to medium, melt the butter in the skillet and cook the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the peas and 2 tbsp water and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until hot, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Return the gnocchi to the pan with the lemon zest, lemon juice, salt and pepper and toss well.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in half the parmesan and serve topped with the rest.

name: Pesto tortellini with blistered cherry tomatoes
side: Garlic bread or a simple green salad.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the salt.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the cherry tomatoes for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan, until blistered and starting to burst; add the garlic for the last 30 seconds.
Cook the tortellini according to the package, usually 2 to 3 minutes, then scoop out ½ cup of the cooking water and drain.

Add the tortellini, spinach, pesto, lemon juice and ¼ cup of the cooking water to the skillet and toss over low heat until the spinach wilts and the sauce is glossy, adding more water if it looks dry.
Serve sprinkled with the parmesan.

name: Mushroom stroganoff with egg noodles
side: Steamed green beans or a crisp cucumber salad.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with half the salt for the noodles.
Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until browned and their liquid has cooked off.
Add the remaining butter and the onion and cook for 3 minutes, then stir in the garlic and paprika for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute, then whisk in the broth, soy sauce and Dijon and simmer for 3 minutes, until thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the egg noodles for 6 to 7 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the sour cream, the rest of the salt and the pepper; don't let it boil once the sour cream is in or it may split.
Serve the stroganoff over the noodles, scattered with parsley.

name: Corn and tofu egg drop soup
steps: Bring the broth, ginger and soy sauce to a boil in a large pot over high heat.
Add the corn and tofu and simmer for 4 minutes, until the corn is hot.
Whisk the cornstarch with ¼ cup cold water, stir it into the soup and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, until slightly thickened.

Turn the heat down so the soup barely simmers, stir it in a slow circle and drizzle in the beaten eggs in a thin stream; leave for 30 seconds, then stir gently so the eggs set into ribbons and are cooked through.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and pepper and serve topped with the scallions.

name: Stir-fried soba with tofu and snap peas
side: Sliced cucumbers with a splash of rice vinegar.

ingredients.note: patted dry, cut into ¾-inch cubes

steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil for the soba.

Toss the tofu with the cornstarch, heat 1½ tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tofu for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides; set it aside on a plate.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Cook the soba for about 4 minutes, following the package, then drain and rinse under cold water so it doesn't stick.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet and stir-fry the snap peas and carrots for 3 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Add the soba, tofu and sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until everything is hot and coated.
Serve topped with the scallions.

name: Tex-Mex migas with peppers
mildNote: Leave out the jalapeño (or cook it only into one side of the pan) and use mild salsa.
steps: Beat the eggs with the salt in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and cook the onion, bell pepper and jalapeño for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, then stir in the tortilla chips for 1 minute so they soften slightly.
Pour in the eggs, turn the heat to medium-low and stir gently for 3 to 4 minutes, until softly set with no liquid egg left.
Scatter the cheddar over the top, cover for 1 minute to melt, then take the pan off the heat.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side and serve the migas in them with the salsa and cilantro.

name: Creamy roasted red pepper rigatoni
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with most of the salt and cook the rigatoni for 11 to 12 minutes, until al dente; scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Blend the onion mixture with the roasted peppers, cream cheese and the rest of the salt in a blender (or with a stick blender in a tall jug) until smooth, then pour it back into the skillet.
Stir in the parmesan and ½ cup of the pasta water and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the drained rigatoni and the spinach and toss until the spinach wilts, loosening with more pasta water if needed.
Serve scattered with the basil.

name: Chili paneer with peppers and onions
mildNote: Leave the sriracha out of the sauce and pass it at the table for anyone who wants heat.
steps: Toss the paneer with 2 tbsp of the cornstarch.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and fry the paneer for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides; set aside on a plate.
Whisk the soy sauce, sriracha, rice vinegar, sugar, the remaining 1 tbsp cornstarch and ½ cup water in a small bowl.
Add the remaining oil to the skillet and stir-fry the onion and bell peppers for 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp-tender, then add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and let it bubble for 1 minute, until glossy and thick, then return the paneer and toss to coat.
Warm the naan in a dry skillet for about 1 minute per side and serve with the chili paneer, topped with the scallions.

name: Fettuccine Alfredo with broccoli
side: Sliced tomatoes with a pinch of salt.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the salt and cook the fettuccine for 10 to 11 minutes, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes; scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat and cook the garlic for 1 minute without browning.
Add the cream and simmer gently for 4 to 5 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Take the skillet off the heat and whisk in the parmesan, nutmeg and pepper until smooth.
Add the fettuccine and broccoli and toss, adding splashes of the cooking water until the sauce coats the pasta; serve right away.

name: Herb and goat cheese omelets
side: Arugula and tomato salad with baguette.
steps: Toss the arugula and cherry tomatoes with the olive oil, lemon juice and a pinch of the salt, and slice the baguette.
Beat the eggs with the rest of the salt, the pepper, parsley and scallions until no streaks of white remain.
Melt ½ tbsp of the butter in an 8- to 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat and pour in a quarter of the eggs (about ¾ cup).
Stir gently with a spatula for 30 seconds, then let it cook undisturbed for 1 to 2 minutes, until the top is just set with no runny egg.
Scatter a quarter of the goat cheese over one half, fold the omelet over and slide it onto a plate; cover loosely with foil.
Repeat with the remaining butter, eggs and goat cheese to make 4 omelets, and serve with the salad and baguette.

name: Thai red curry pumpkin soup with chickpeas
mildNote: Use 1 tbsp curry paste for a mild, sweet soup, and stir a little extra paste into adult bowls if you like.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and curry paste and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin, broth, brown sugar, salt and all but 3 tbsp of the coconut milk, stir until smooth and bring to a simmer.
Add the chickpeas and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn't catch on the bottom.
Meanwhile, warm the naan in a dry skillet for about 1 minute per side.
Stir in the lime juice, then serve the soup drizzled with the saved coconut milk and topped with cilantro, with the naan on the side.

name: Hoisin tofu lettuce wraps

ingredients.note: sliced, white and green parts kept apart

steps: Press the tofu in a clean towel to squeeze out as much water as you can, then crumble it into small pieces.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tofu for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden and dry.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until browned, then stir in the garlic, ginger and scallion whites for 1 minute.
Stir in the hoisin, soy sauce and rice vinegar and cook for 1 minute, until the filling is glossy.
Spoon the filling into the lettuce leaves and top with the carrots, scallion greens and peanuts.

name: Mediterranean hummus naan pizzas
side: Cucumber slices and a green salad.
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F and set the naan on a large sheet pan.
Toss the spinach with the olive oil.
Spread the hummus over the naan, almost to the edges, then pile on the spinach, mozzarella, cherry tomatoes, red onion, olives and feta.
Sprinkle with the oregano and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese has melted and the edges are crisp.
Cut each naan into wedges and serve hot.

name: Loaded black bean sheet-pan nachos
side: Fresh pico de gallo and mashed avocado on top.
mildNote: Leave the jalapeño out of the pico and halve the chili powder.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and toss the black beans and corn with the cumin, chili powder and half the salt.
Spread half the tortilla chips on a large sheet pan, scatter over half the beans and corn and half the cheddar, then repeat the layers.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese has melted and the edges of the chips are toasted.
Meanwhile, stir the tomatoes, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro and half the lime juice together for a quick pico de gallo.
Mash the avocados with the rest of the lime juice and salt.
Spoon the pico, mashed avocado and sour cream over the hot nachos and serve straight from the pan.

name: Penne with artichokes, olives and roasted peppers
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the salt and cook the penne for 10 to 11 minutes, until al dente; scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the garlic and oregano for 1 minute, until the garlic is pale gold.
Add the artichokes, roasted peppers and olives and cook for 3 minutes, until hot and the artichokes start to brown at the edges.
Add the drained penne, lemon zest, lemon juice and ½ cup of the cooking water and toss until glossy.
Take the pan off the heat, fold in the arugula and parsley, and serve topped with the feta.

name: Crispy tofu banh mi sandwiches
side: Extra quick-pickled carrots and cucumber spears.
mildNote: Use plain mayo for kids' sandwiches and leave out the jalapeño.

ingredients.note: patted dry, cut into ½-inch slabs

steps: Stir the rice vinegar, sugar, salt and ¼ cup warm water in a bowl until dissolved, add the carrots and leave them to pickle while you cook.
Brush the tofu slabs with the soy sauce, then dust both sides with the cornstarch.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until crisp and golden, in two batches if needed.
Stir the mayo and sriracha together, and toast the split rolls cut side down in the skillet or under the broiler for 1 to 2 minutes.
Spread the rolls with the sriracha mayo and fill with the tofu, drained pickled carrots, cucumber, jalapeño and cilantro.

name: Greek chickpea salad pitas
steps: Stir the yogurt with the garlic, half the dill, half the lemon juice and a pinch of the salt to make a quick sauce.
Put the chickpeas in a large bowl and lightly mash about half of them with a fork.
Add the cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, olives, olive oil, oregano, the remaining dill, lemon juice and salt and toss well, then fold in the feta.
Warm the pitas in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, then cut them in half and open the pockets.
Spread a spoonful of the yogurt sauce inside each pocket and stuff with the chickpea salad, with extra sauce on the side.

name: Smashed pinto bean tostadas
mildNote: Leave out the chili powder and use mild salsa.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F, brush the tortillas on both sides with 2 tbsp of the oil and spread them over two sheet pans.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, flipping halfway, until crisp and golden.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic, cumin and chili powder for 30 seconds.
Add the pinto beans and ¼ cup water, mash them well and cook for 3 minutes, until thick and spreadable; season with half the salt.
Toss the cabbage with the lime juice and the rest of the salt.
Spread the beans over the tostadas and top with the cabbage, avocado, salsa and feta; serve with the lime wedges.

name: Cheddar corn fritters with salsa
side: Sliced tomatoes and a green salad.
steps: Rinse the frozen corn under warm water to thaw it, then pat it very dry on a towel.
Whisk the eggs and milk in a large bowl, then stir in the flour, cornmeal, salt and smoked paprika until just combined.
Fold in the corn, cheddar and scallions.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat, drop in ¼-cup scoops of batter, flatten them slightly and cook for about 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and the centers spring back when pressed.
Move the fritters to a paper-towel-lined plate and repeat with the rest of the batter, adding more oil between batches.
Serve hot with the salsa and sour cream.

name: Ginger-scallion noodles with bok choy and fried eggs
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the noodles.
Put the scallions, ginger and salt in a heatproof bowl, heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers, then carefully pour it over (it will sizzle) and stir.
Stir the soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar and sugar into the ginger-scallion oil.
Cook the egg noodles for 5 to 6 minutes, adding the bok choy for the last 2 minutes, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and fry the eggs for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are completely set.
Toss the noodles and bok choy with the ginger-scallion sauce and serve each bowl topped with a fried egg.

name: Honey garlic chicken bites with peppers
side: Cucumber salad, or rice if you have some cooked.
steps: Toss the chicken with the cornstarch, salt and pepper (don't rinse raw chicken; wash your hands and board after handling it).
Whisk the honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic and 2 tbsp water in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir-fry the bell peppers for 3 minutes, until crisp-tender; set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the chicken in a single layer and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden and the thickest pieces reach 165°F.
Pour in the sauce and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Return the peppers, toss, and serve topped with the scallions and sesame seeds.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss cubed tofu in cornstarch, fry it in a small pan until golden, then toss with a few spoonfuls of the sauce before it goes in with the chicken.

name: Chicken club wraps
steps: Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat for 7 to 8 minutes, until crisp, then drain on paper towels and pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the fat (add the olive oil if the pan looks dry).
Season the chicken cutlets with the garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken in the skillet over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and 165°F in the thickest part, then rest it for 3 minutes and slice.
Stir the mayo and Dijon together, and warm the tortillas in the skillet or microwave so they roll without cracking.
Spread each tortilla with the Dijon mayo, add romaine, tomato, avocado, sliced chicken and crumbled bacon, then roll up tightly and cut in half.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, mash a can of chickpeas with a spoonful of the Dijon mayo and roll it up with the vegetables instead of the chicken and bacon.

name: Creamy Cajun chicken penne
mildNote: Leave out the cayenne; the paprika gives color and flavor without heat.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add about half the salt and cook the penne for 10 to 11 minutes; scoop out ½ cup of the cooking water before draining.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, cayenne and the rest of the salt, and toss the chicken in it.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6 to 7 minutes, turning, until browned and 165°F inside; move it to a plate.
Add the bell pepper to the skillet and cook for 3 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the half-and-half and simmer for 3 minutes, until slightly thickened, then stir in the parmesan.
Return the chicken with the drained penne and toss, adding pasta water as needed for a creamy sauce.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, before the chicken goes back in, spoon some pasta and sauce into a small pan and stir in a can of white beans until hot.

name: Fresh orange chicken with broccoli
side: Sliced cucumbers, or rice if you have some cooked.
steps: Whisk the orange zest and juice, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger and 1 tbsp of the cornstarch in a bowl.
Toss the chicken with the remaining cornstarch (don't rinse raw chicken; wash your hands after handling it).
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the broccoli and 3 tbsp water, cover and cook for 3 minutes, until bright green and crisp-tender; set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the chicken in a single layer and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden and 165°F inside.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Return the broccoli, toss, and serve topped with the scallions and sesame seeds.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, fry cubed tofu tossed in cornstarch in a small pan until golden, then toss it with a few spoonfuls of the orange sauce.

name: Chicken Milanese with lemony arugula

ingredients.note: halved horizontally and pounded ¼ inch thin

steps: Set out three shallow dishes: the flour mixed with half the salt and the pepper, the beaten eggs, and the panko mixed with the parmesan.
Dip each cutlet in flour, then egg, then the panko mix, pressing so it sticks; wash your hands after handling the raw chicken.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry two cutlets for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and 165°F inside; drain on paper towels.
Add 2 more tbsp of oil and fry the remaining cutlets the same way.
Toss the arugula and cherry tomatoes with the last 2 tbsp of oil, the lemon juice and the rest of the salt.
Serve each cutlet topped with a pile of the salad, with the lemon wedges on the side.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, bread ½-inch slices of eggplant the same way and fry them in a clean pan first, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until tender.

name: Chipotle chicken and pepper quesadillas
side: Cilantro sour cream and a quick corn salad.
mildNote: Leave the chipotle out of the filling and stir a little into the adults' sour cream instead.
steps: Toss the chicken with the cumin and salt; don't rinse raw chicken, and wash your hands after handling it.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6 to 7 minutes, until browned and 165°F inside.
Add the bell pepper and onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft, then stir in the chipotle and half the lime juice for 30 seconds; scrape into a bowl and wipe out the skillet.
Sprinkle half of each tortilla with cheese, add the filling, top with more cheese and fold over.
Brush the skillet with the remaining oil and cook the quesadillas two at a time over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and melted.
Stir the sour cream with the cilantro and the rest of the lime juice and serve with the quesadillas, cut into wedges.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a can of pinto beans with a pinch of the cumin in a small pan, mash, and use as the filling in a couple of the quesadillas, cooked first in a clean pan.

name: Creamy garlic mushroom chicken
side: Crusty bread and a green salad.
steps: Season the chicken with the salt and pepper and dust it lightly with the flour.
Heat the oil and 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and 165°F inside; move it to a plate.
Add the remaining butter and the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes, until browned, then stir in the shallots, garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer for 3 minutes, until reduced by about a third.
Stir in the cream and Dijon and simmer for 2 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon.
Return the chicken and any juices, simmer for 1 minute, and serve scattered with parsley.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, spoon some of the mushroom sauce into a small pan before the chicken goes back in, add a can of white beans and simmer until hot.

name: Chicken caprese skillet
side: Toasted baguette and a green salad.
steps: Season the chicken with the Italian seasoning, most of the salt and the pepper; wash your hands after handling the raw chicken.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and 165°F inside.
Top each cutlet with mozzarella slices, cover the pan for 1 to 2 minutes until the cheese melts, then move the chicken to plates.
Add the cherry tomatoes and garlic to the skillet and cook for 3 minutes, until the tomatoes burst, then stir in the vinegar and the rest of the salt.
Spoon the tomatoes over the chicken, scatter with the basil and serve with the toasted baguette.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a can of white beans with a few of the burst tomatoes in a small pan and top with a slice of the mozzarella.

name: Egg roll in a bowl with rice noodles
side: Sriracha and extra soy sauce at the table.

ingredients.note: sliced, white and green parts kept apart

steps: Soak the rice noodles in a bowl of very hot tap water for 8 to 10 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left and 160°F.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and scallion whites and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cabbage and carrots and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until wilted but still a little crisp.
Stir in the soy sauce and rice vinegar, then toss in the noodles until hot.
Drizzle with the sesame oil and serve topped with the scallion greens.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, fry crumbled tofu in a small pan until golden, then add a share of the cabbage and carrots and a splash of soy sauce before the cabbage goes in with the pork.

name: Pork chops with apples and Dijon pan sauce
steps: Pat the pork chops dry and season both sides with the salt, pepper and thyme.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear the chops for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and 145°F in the center; move them to a plate and rest for 3 minutes.
Turn the heat to medium, melt the butter and cook the apples and onion for 5 minutes, until golden and tender.
Pour in the broth and cider vinegar, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the Dijon and cream and simmer for 1 minute, then return the chops and their juices and spoon the sauce over.

name: Five-spice pork medallions with green beans
side: Sliced cucumbers, or noodles if you like.
steps: Season the pork medallions all over with the five-spice and salt.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear the pork for about 3 minutes per side, until browned and 145°F in the center; move it to a plate and rest for 3 minutes.

Add the remaining oil, the green beans and 3 tbsp water, cover and cook for 3 minutes, then uncover and cook 2 minutes more, until crisp-tender and lightly blistered; stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Whisk the hoisin, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar and 2 tbsp water, pour it into the pan and let it bubble for 1 minute.
Return the pork and its juices and toss to coat, then serve topped with the scallions and sesame seeds.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, sear slices of tofu in a small pan until golden and toss them with a spoonful of the sauce and some of the green beans.

name: Sausage tortellini in tomato cream sauce
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the sausage and onion for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking up the sausage, until browned with no pink left and 160°F.
Stir in the garlic and Italian seasoning for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the tortellini according to the package, usually 2 to 3 minutes, and drain.
Stir the cream into the sauce, add the spinach and stir until wilted, then fold in the tortellini.
Serve sprinkled with the parmesan.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a cup of marinara in a small pan and toss a share of the tortellini in it with some parmesan.

name: Kielbasa with buttered cabbage and noodles
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with a pinch of the salt.

Melt 3 tbsp of the butter in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion and cabbage with the rest of the salt for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until tender and golden at the edges.
Meanwhile, melt the remaining butter in a second skillet over medium-high heat and brown the kielbasa for 4 to 5 minutes, until sizzling and hot all the way through.
Cook the egg noodles for 6 to 7 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Stir the garlic and paprika into the cabbage for 30 seconds, then add the vinegar, noodles and pepper and toss.
Fold in the kielbasa and serve.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, scoop out a portion of the cabbage and noodles before the kielbasa goes in and top it with a fried egg.

name: Chorizo and chickpeas with spinach
mildNote: Look for a mild chorizo; the smoked paprika adds smokiness, not heat.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the chorizo for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and 160°F; spoon off all but about 1 tbsp of the fat.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until soft, then stir in the garlic and smoked paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas and ½ cup water and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then scatter with the parsley.
Warm the bread in a low oven or toast it, and serve with the chorizo and chickpeas.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a can of chickpeas in a small pan with a little olive oil, garlic and smoked paprika, then stir in a handful of the spinach.

name: Spaghetti carbonara with peas
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the salt and cook the spaghetti for 9 to 10 minutes, adding the peas for the last minute.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until crisp; turn off the heat and pour off all but about 2 tbsp of the fat.
Whisk the 2 eggs, 2 yolks, parmesan and pepper in a bowl.
Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water, drain the spaghetti and peas, and add them to the skillet with the bacon; toss well.

Pour in the egg mixture with ¼ cup of the hot pasta water, tossing quickly, then set the pan over low heat and keep tossing for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce thickens into a creamy coating and no runny egg remains (add more pasta water if it gets too thick).
Serve right away with extra pepper.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, toss a share of the spaghetti and peas in a small pan with butter and a little of the egg-parmesan mixture over low heat until creamy.

name: Smash burger tacos
steps: Stir the mayo, Dijon and paprika together for the burger sauce.
Press each ball of beef very thin over one side of a tortilla, right to the edges, then sprinkle with the onion, salt and pepper; wash your hands after handling the raw beef.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tacos beef side down, two or three at a time, for 3 to 4 minutes, until the beef is well browned and cooked through to 160°F.
Flip so the tortilla side is down, scatter the cheddar over the beef and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the tortilla is crisp and the cheese melts.
Repeat with the rest, then top with the burger sauce, romaine and tomatoes, fold and serve.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, mash a can of black beans with a pinch of paprika, press it onto a couple of tortillas and cook them first in a clean pan the same way.

name: Garlic butter steak bites with asparagus
side: Baguette slices to mop up the butter.

ingredients.note: woody ends snapped off, cut into 2-inch pieces

steps: Pat the steak dry and season it with most of the salt and the pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the asparagus with the rest of the salt for 4 to 5 minutes, until bright green and crisp-tender; set aside.
Add the remaining oil and sear the steak in a single layer, in two batches if needed, for about 2 minutes per side, until browned and 145°F inside.
Turn the heat to medium, add the butter and garlic and cook for 1 minute, then return the asparagus and toss everything in the garlic butter.
Let it rest for 3 minutes off the heat, then scatter with parsley and serve with the lemon wedges and baguette.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, brown thickly sliced mushrooms in a small pan with a pat of the butter and some garlic.

name: One-pot cheeseburger macaroni
side: Steamed green beans or a green salad.
steps: Brown the beef and onion in a large, deep skillet or pot over medium-high heat for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F; spoon off excess fat.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the broth, milk, Worcestershire, Dijon, salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Stir in the macaroni, cover, turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the cheddar until melted and let it sit for 2 minutes to thicken before serving.

name: Mongolian-style beef noodles

ingredients.note: very thinly sliced against the grain

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the egg noodles for 6 minutes, until tender; drain.
Toss the steak with the cornstarch, and whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar and ½ cup water in a bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear the beef in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until browned with no pink left (at least 145°F); move it to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the carrots and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and simmer for 2 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Return the beef with the scallions and noodles and toss for 1 minute, until everything is coated and hot.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, fry cubed tofu tossed in a little cornstarch in a small pan until golden, then toss with some noodles and a few spoonfuls of the sauce before the beef goes back in.

name: Quick turkey and zucchini spaghetti
side: Garlic bread or a green salad.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add most of the salt and cook the spaghetti for 9 to 10 minutes; scoop out ½ cup of the cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the turkey and onion for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F.
Add the zucchini and the rest of the salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until just tender.
Stir in the garlic and Italian seasoning for 30 seconds, then add the marinara and simmer for 5 minutes.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce, loosening it with pasta water if needed, and serve with the parmesan and basil.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a can of white beans with a cup of marinara in a small pan and spoon it over their spaghetti.

name: Spiced lamb over hummus with chopped salad
side: Warm pita and the chopped salad.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the lamb and onion for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking up the meat, until browned with no pink left and 160°F; spoon off excess fat.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, cinnamon and most of the salt with 2 tbsp water and cook for 1 minute.
Toss the cucumber, tomatoes and parsley with the lemon juice and the rest of the salt.
Warm the pitas in a dry skillet for about 30 seconds per side.
Spread the hummus in shallow bowls, spoon the lamb over the top and serve with the chopped salad and warm pita.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a can of chickpeas with a pinch each of the cumin, paprika and cinnamon in a small pan and spoon it over the hummus.

name: Seared salmon Caesar salad
steps: Whisk the mayo, lemon juice, Dijon, garlic, Worcestershire, half the parmesan, half the pepper and 1 tbsp water into a dressing.
Toast the bread cubes in a large skillet with 1 tbsp of the oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until golden; set aside.
Season the salmon with the salt and the rest of the pepper, add the remaining oil to the skillet and turn the heat to medium-high.
Cook the salmon flesh side down for 4 minutes, flip and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until it reaches 145°F or flakes easily with a fork.
Toss the romaine with the dressing, croutons and remaining parmesan and serve topped with the salmon.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a can of chickpeas in a small pan with a little olive oil until crisp at the edges, and dress their salad with lemon and olive oil instead of the Caesar dressing, which contains Worcestershire.

name: Lemon cream fettuccine with salmon and peas
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with most of the salt.

Season the salmon with the rest of the salt and the pepper, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook it for about 4 minutes per side, until 145°F or it flakes easily; move to a plate and break into large flakes, discarding any skin.
Cook the fettuccine for 10 to 11 minutes, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes; scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile, wipe out the skillet, melt the butter over medium heat and cook the garlic for 1 minute, then add the half-and-half and lemon zest and simmer for 2 minutes.
Whisk in the parmesan, then add the pasta, peas, lemon juice and a splash of the cooking water and toss until creamy.
Gently fold in the salmon and dill and serve.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, serve a portion before the salmon goes in and top it with a can of white beans warmed in a small pan.

name: Cod with brown butter, capers and lemon couscous
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a saucepan, stir in the couscous and peas, cover and take off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and stir in the lemon zest and the juice of 1 lemon.
Season the cod with the salt and pepper and dust it lightly with the flour.
Heat the oil and 1 tbsp of the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook the cod for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and 145°F or it flakes easily; move to plates.
Turn the heat to medium, add the remaining butter and swirl for 2 to 3 minutes, until it foams and smells nutty and golden brown.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the capers, the juice of the second lemon and the parsley, and spoon the brown butter over the cod; serve with the couscous.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a can of chickpeas in a separate small pan with a tablespoon of butter and a squeeze of lemon and serve over the couscous.

name: Red curry coconut tilapia with spinach
mildNote: Use 2 teaspoons of curry paste; the coconut milk keeps it gentle, and adults can stir in more.
steps: Soak the rice noodles in very hot tap water for 8 to 10 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat and cook the garlic, ginger and curry paste for 1 minute.
Stir in the coconut milk and brown sugar and simmer for 2 minutes.
Season the tilapia with the salt, stir the fish sauce into the sauce and nestle in the fillets; cover and simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes, until the fish reaches 145°F and flakes easily.
Push the spinach into the sauce around the fish until it wilts, then stir in the lime juice.
Serve the fish and sauce over the noodles, scattered with cilantro.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, ladle some of the coconut curry sauce into a small pan before the fish sauce and fish go in, and simmer tofu cubes and a handful of the spinach in it.

name: Chili-lime shrimp tacos with avocado salsa
side: Black beans or a quick corn salad.
mildNote: Halve the chili powder; it's earthy rather than hot, and the sour cream cools it further.
steps: If the shrimp are frozen, thaw them in a colander under cold running water for 5 minutes, then pat dry.
Gently mix the avocado, tomatoes, red onion, cilantro, the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of the salt for the salsa, and toss the cabbage with the juice of another lime.
Toss the shrimp with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and the rest of the salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp in a single layer for about 2 minutes per side, until pink and opaque all the way through, then squeeze over the last lime.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for about 30 seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with the cabbage, shrimp and avocado salsa and top with sour cream.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, warm a can of black beans with a pinch of the spices in a small pan and use them in place of the shrimp.

name: Shrimp po' boys
side: Coleslaw or pickles on the side.
mildNote: Leave out the cayenne; the paprika coating is mild.
steps: Stir the mayo, Dijon, lemon juice and a pinch of the paprika together for the sauce.
Put the beaten eggs in one bowl and mix the flour, cornmeal, the rest of the paprika, the cayenne and salt in another.
Dip the shrimp in the egg, then roll them in the cornmeal mixture.

Heat the oil (about ¼ inch deep) in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers, about 350°F, and fry the shrimp in batches for 1½ to 2 minutes per side, until golden and opaque all the way through; drain on paper towels.
Toast the split rolls, spread with the sauce, and fill with the romaine, tomato and shrimp.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, coat slices of tofu in the same egg and cornmeal mixture and fry them first, before the shrimp, until golden.

name: Smoky shrimp, kielbasa and corn skillet
mildNote: Leave out the cayenne; smoked paprika is not hot.
steps: Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the kielbasa for 4 minutes.
Add the onion and bell peppers and cook for 4 minutes, then add the corn and cook 3 minutes more, until hot.
Stir in the remaining butter, garlic, smoked paprika, thyme and cayenne for 30 seconds.
Add the shrimp and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until pink and opaque all the way through.
Squeeze in the lemon juice, scatter with parsley and serve with the crusty bread.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, sauté a share of the corn and peppers in a separate small pan with butter, a pinch of the smoked paprika and a can of white beans until hot.

name: Tuscan tuna and white bean salad with garlic toasts
side: Garlic toasts (made in the recipe) and olives.
steps: Put the red onion in a large bowl with the vinegar, lemon juice and salt and let it sit for 5 minutes to soften.
Whisk in the Dijon, 3 tbsp of the olive oil and the pepper.
Add the white beans, cherry tomatoes and parsley, then the tuna in large chunks, and toss gently.
Brush the bread with the remaining oil and toast it in a skillet over medium heat for about 2 minutes per side, until golden, then rub with the cut garlic.
Fold the arugula into the salad just before serving with the garlic toasts.

vegetarianSwap.note: For vegetarians, scoop out some salad before the tuna goes in and add an extra can of white beans to it.
